name: Mango Sticky Rice Horchata

ingredients.name: uncooked white jasmine rice, rinsed until water runs clear
fresh lime juice, from 1 large lime

instructions.primary_message: In a large bowl, combine rice, cardamom, and 3 cups water. Cover, refrigerate, and let rice soak until starch is released and grains have softened slightly, at least 8 hours or up to 12 hours.

Set a fine-mesh strainer over a large bowl. Transfer soaked rice and soaking liquid to blender and blend on high until completely smooth, about 2 minutes. Pour mixture through prepared strainer, scraping bottom of strainer with spoon or rubber spatula to help liquid pass through. Discard solids.

Rinse strainer, then line it with cheesecloth and set it over a clean large bowl. Pour strained rice liquid through prepared strainer, scraping bottom of strainer to help liquid pass through. Discard any remaining solids. You should have about 2 1/2 cups rice liquid.

Rinse blender. Add mango, condensed milk, coconut milk, lime juice, vanilla, salt, remaining 1 cup water, and strained rice liquid. Process until completely smooth, about 2 minutes. Transfer to a pitcher and refrigerate until very cold, about 1 hour.
Stir before serving. Pour over ice. Top with fresh mango and toasted coconut, if using. Serve.

schema_metadata.keywords: mango sticky rice horchata, mango horchata, coconut horchata, jasmine rice, mango drink, horchata, mango smoothie

description: This creamy mango sticky rice horchata blends jasmine rice, ripe mango, coconut milk, and cardamom into a refreshing summer drink.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 8 hr 15 min.

Optional or for serving: Toasted unsweetened coconut flakes, for serving (optional)

Notes: An equal weight of thawed frozen mango can be used in place of the fresh mango. Frozen Alphonso mango purée or canned Alphonso mango pulp can also be substituted; use 283 g. Check the ingredient list, as some brands contain added sugar and may make the horchata sweeter.

Make-ahead and storage: Horchata can be made up to 2 days in advance. Top with mango and coconut, if using, just before serving.
author: Laila Ibrahim
